svg.title: Retry storms are self-inflicted. Jitter, a bucket and a breaker.
svg.desc: Two timelines: without jitter a thousand retries land in one dense column exactly one second after the upstream failed and knock it over again; with full jitter the same retries are spread across the window and the upstream stays up. Below, the backoff formula with uniform(0, ...) circled, a token bucket metering eight tokens a second, a three-state circuit breaker, and bars comparing a naive client at 285 of 400 in 0.16 s, a retrying client at 358 of 400 with 185 rate-limit errors, and a bucketed client at 400 of 400 with none.
svg.text: Retry storms are self-inflicted. Jitter, a bucket and a breaker.
same total wait, spread across the window
empty bucket = you wait. Set it just UNDER
a retried POST double-charges the customer
OPEN means fail INSTANTLY. Do not queue - the point is
to stop sending, not to wait politely.
...and what does a retry cost the SERVER?
